content.value_statement: Vague UI prompts often produce inconsistent Stitch screens. This skill turns rough ideas into structured prompts with design system context, UI vocabulary, and clear page sections.
actual_capabilities: Assesses prompts for missing platform, page type, structure, visual style, colors, and components.
Reads DESIGN.md when present and includes palette, typography, and component guidance.
Adds UI and UX keywords that describe concrete components and layouts.
Formats enhanced prompts with design system sections and numbered page structure.
Can write the enhanced prompt to next-prompt.md or a user-specified file when requested.
Directs users to Stitch prompting documentation for current guidance.
limitations: It improves prompts; it does not generate the final interface itself.
It depends on the quality and accuracy of the original user intent.
It may infer missing design choices when the request lacks detail.
It targets Stitch workflows and may need adjustment for other builders.

use_cases.title: Clarify Early UI Ideas
use_cases.description: Turn a short screen idea into a structured Stitch prompt with platform, sections, style, colors, and components.

use_cases.title: Keep Screens Consistent
use_cases.description: Use an existing DESIGN.md file so new screen prompts follow the same visual system.

use_cases.title: Improve Regeneration Requests
use_cases.description: Rewrite failed or vague UI generation requests into focused edits that preserve existing screen intent.

prompt_templates.title: Improve a Basic Screen Idea
prompt_templates.prompt: Enhance this Stitch prompt: [describe the screen]. Add platform, visual style, sections, colors, and component keywords.

prompt_templates.title: Apply a Design System
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the current DESIGN.md to enhance this prompt: [prompt]. Keep the design system required and make assumptions explicit.

prompt_templates.title: Refine a Failed Generation
prompt_templates.prompt: My Stitch result missed these points: [issues]. Rewrite the prompt to correct them while preserving the original product intent.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a Multi-Screen Flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Create enhanced Stitch prompts for these screens: [screens]. Use shared design guidance, clear navigation context, and one prompt per screen.

output_examples.output: A structured login page prompt with a clear platform, professional light theme, form card, labeled fields, primary button, and footer link.
A focused edit prompt that places a search input in the header, defines style, icon, placeholder text, width, and focus behavior.

output_examples.input: create a dashboard for orders using our design system
output_examples.output: A dashboard prompt that includes DESIGN.md guidance, metric cards, order tables, filters, navigation, and responsive layout details.

best_practices: Provide the product goal, target device, and core user action before asking for enhancement.
Keep DESIGN.md current so prompts use consistent colors, type, and components.
Use one focused edit request when refining an existing Stitch screen.
anti_patterns: Asking for many unrelated screens in one vague prompt.
Omitting brand, audience, and platform details when they are important.
Treating inferred design choices as final without reviewing them.

faq.question: Does this skill generate UI code?
faq.answer: No. It prepares stronger prompts for Stitch and leaves implementation to the generation tool.

faq.question: Does it require DESIGN.md?
faq.answer: No. It uses DESIGN.md when present and adds a consistency tip when it is missing.

faq.question: Can it write files?
faq.answer: Yes. It can write the enhanced prompt to a requested markdown file.

faq.question: Is it only for Stitch?
faq.answer: It is optimized for Stitch. The prompt structure may still help other UI generation tools.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, and Claude Code use it?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill metadata lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What input works best?
faq.answer: Share the screen goal, target users, platform, desired style, and any existing design constraints.
